A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSV-C/TSV-M research and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-merging and compression results in Tables 2–3, ablations in Tables 4–6, and further empirical analyses in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations and appendix analyses. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same singular-vector decomposition, truncation, task-specific compression and whitening/Procrustes merging procedure. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nested suites of 8, 14 and 20 classification datasets and the same additional task subsets in Appendix B.2. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets in Tables 2–3 are unchanged, including Task Arithmetic, Consensus TA and TALL-Mask+TIES. Figure 1 changes 'Task Vector' to 'Task Arithmetic'; its 84.93/79.41/74.01 scores already match that Table 2 baseline in v1.

E3.justification: Both retain the same three CLIP ViT configurations, reused checkpoints, absolute and normalized accuracy metrics, batch size of 32, scaling-factor search and task-subset evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain the same component ablations, rank sensitivity, orthogonalization-error distributions, per-layer interference, scaling-factor analysis and confusion matrices. Restyling these displays adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing averages and layerwise error distributions use unchanged reporting practices.

E6.justification: Benchmark and ablation entries, plotted data and qualitative findings are retained. For example, TSV-M's ViT-L-14 accuracy remains 92.98, 89.17 and 87.72 for 8, 14 and 20 tasks in Table 2. Recoloring and tick formatting do not change results.

T1.justification: The STI definition, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 6.1, Appendix A example, Appendix B.3 storage derivation and Appendix C proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: low-rank task structure, compression to 10% of original size while retaining 99% accuracy, and improved merging through interference reduction.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations connecting truncation to lower orthogonalization error and early-layer shared features to greater interference. Discussions of scaling-factor tuning, compression applicability and alternatives to uniform task ranks are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B and D retain the same implementation, hardware, hyperparameters, checkpoint reuse and numerical-stabilization details. The code-access link is identical.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, 51 references and positioning relative to earlier merging and compression methods are unchanged. Figure 1's baseline-label correction introduces no different cited method.

P1.justification: Small edits correct '20 task' to '20 tasks' in Tables 2–3, standardize figure labels and remove the redundant 'figure' before 'Fig. 7' in Appendix B.2. The prose and section organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 changes palettes throughout the plots, including heatmaps, radar plots and confusion matrices, and adjusts grids and labels in Figures 1 and 5. These are styling refinements to existing displays; plotted content, panel arrangements and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Scientific evidence, theoretical support and reproducibility information are unchanged. Correcting Figure 1's baseline name offers a small clarity benefit, but recoloring leaves captions describing blue curves that are now green in Figures 2, 11, 12 and 16. These limited presentation tradeoffs produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
